source_observations.observation: SupportIQ is a fictional CloudDesk B2B support portal for a demonstrable learning release, not a production-readiness commitment; the source defines synthetic data and a mandatory first-release scope with explicit deferrals.

The four predefined roles are Platform Admin, Tenant Admin, Support Manager, and Support Agent. The assistant is listed for these internal roles; retrieval and analytics are subject to tenant/team/role scope, default-deny authorization, and minimized Platform Admin access.

Knowledge retrieval is approval- and version-gated; AI outputs are assistive, grounded, validated, allowlisted, and non-mutating; evaluation targets are measurement targets, while unauthorized access is a mandatory failure.

The source defines local identity, role/resource/action permissions, independent approval of privileged Platform Admin changes, tenant/team ticket workflows, correction/cancellation requests, persisted asynchronous jobs, restricted transactional email, audit, retention, test, and deployment expectations.

Exact AI deployment/region, model-specific token and monetary budgets, email provider/sender, and per-operation background timeout/retry values are explicitly open/deferred. Retention values are proposed configurable defaults and are not legal or regulatory commitments.
The conversation-history role mapping is not in v1.4. The human selected owner-only history access; this decision is analysis context and must be incorporated through a separate Requirement Update.

source_observations.source: FR-CA-01, FR-CA-02, FR-ID-09, Sections 5.5 and 5.9; current conversation clarification
source_observations.observation: Platform Admin is listed as an assistant user, but routine access to tenant business content is restricted and no Platform Admin tenant-knowledge retrieval scope is stated. The human selected no tenant-content retrieval through the assistant; this decision is not yet incorporated into v1.4.

Feedback submission is specified, but no feedback-read endpoint or permission mapping is defined. The default-deny policy prevents adding a read surface without a separate requirement; this is not a current blocking decision.

assessment.reason: Both required access-scope clarifications were received, but neither is present in the authoritative v1.4 source. The decisions must be incorporated through an authorized immutable Requirement Update, followed by a fresh post-update analysis before independent verification.
